transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 4:00 PM PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Rivera (CTO - Cedar), Priya Singh (Lead ML Engineer), Sara Kim (PM)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Cedar's goals for a PLG/self-serve evaluation of Redwood hosted API and when they'd consider Dedicated/Private.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood PLG team, with Arjun our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:08 - Tom Rivera: Good, thanks. Excited to learn more.
00:12 - Priya Singh: Hi all, quick background - we're building an internal assistant over semantic search, roughly 15qps average peak, but spiky during reporting windows. We're exploring time-to-first-token for devs and cost per 1k tokens.
00:30 - Arjun Patel: Great, that's exactly the sort of workload we've seen. For PLG quickstarts we typically get folks from signup to first token in under an hour; with our free credits you can prototype same day.
00:45 - Sara Kim: When you say free credits, what's included and any usage limits?
00:50 - Maya Chen: The standard PLG grant is $500 in credits that cover hosted inference — good for trying chat, embeddings, and reranking. We'll send details after the call. It's intended to get you to a proof-of-concept quickly.
01:08 - Priya Singh: Cool. For evaluation, our main axes are latency (p50/p95), cost, and controls - especially around data residency and encryption. We're also curious about whether we'll need Dedicated capacity or private deploy.
01:25 - Arjun Patel: Totally. For latency, hosted API on our standard models typically hits ~50-120ms per token on modern GPUs depending on seq length; longer sequences push that up. If you need guaranteed low p95 at scale, Dedicated's reserved capacity is the path we recommend. Private gives you a private control plane and network isolation for compliance-heavy workloads.
01:48 - Tom Rivera: Does Redwood offer any trial for Dedicated or is that always sales-assisted?
01:52 - Maya Chen: Dedicated is usually contract-based, but for evaluation we can provision a small Dedicated trial for a short benchmark if the pilot data justifies it — Arjun can scope that.
02:04 - Arjun Patel: Yep, I can spin up a benchmark harness. Quick note — our runtime does automatic KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated token cost; sometimes the auto cache behavior is subtle with many short-turn prompts.
02:25 - Priya Singh: When you said KV cache, I think our recorder transcribed it as 'K-V cash' earlier, lol, but got it. How does that affect cold-starts?
02:34 - Arjun Patel: Good catch. Cold-starts still pay the initial cost; caching helps with repeated prefixes. For your bursty windows, batching and cache will reduce steady cost but doesn't remove the initial cold RT.
02:48 - Sara Kim: Security — we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and optional customer-managed KMS. Is that all supported?
02:58 - Arjun Patel: Yes, Redwood supports SOC 2, SAML SSO, role based access controls, audit logs, and integrates with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For hosted customers we provide envelope encryption and options to bring-your-own-key in certain tiers — we'll share the exact doc.
03:18 - Tom Rivera: Data residency — we host primarily in us-west, but some of our customers require eu residency. What's your coverage?
03:26 - Maya Chen: We have hosted regions in NA and EU; Private lets you deploy entirely in your VPC in the region you choose. We'll include the regions page in the follow-up.
03:36 - Priya Singh: About model variants — would quantized models impact our latency/quality tradeoffs? We run a few retrieval-augmented generation flows and quality is sensitive.
03:46 - Arjun Patel: Quantized variants can drastically reduce cost and sometimes improve latency for small-batch workloads. Quality regressions are model-dependent; part of the pilot is to compare quality annotations against your eval set. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles based on your evals.
04:05 - Tom Rivera: Our infra guys will want to see network diagrams and the private control plane options.
04:10 - Arjun Patel: I'll attach a sample infra diagram showing VPC peering, Private Control Plane, and optional on-prem connectors.
04:18 - Maya Chen: Let's talk success criteria — Priya, you mentioned p95 latency and cost — any targets?
04:24 - Priya Singh: We're aiming for p50 under 150ms and p95 under 400ms for the main chat path at 99th percentile of our expected pilot QPS (~30 qps). For cost, we'd like to be competitive with our current self-hosted estimate; if Redwood can show unit cost parity or better with caching and batching, that's strong.
04:43 - Maya Chen: That sounds reasonable. For the pilot we'll provision hosted PLG keys with credits and run the benchmark. If results show we need Dedicated, we can scope a small Dedicated eval.
04:53 - Sara Kim: Any gotchas during quickstart? For example, throttling, SDK issues, or tokenization differences?
04:59 - Arjun Patel: Throttling is per-rate-limit on the PLG tier but configurable for enterprise accounts. We do occasionally see SDK version mismatches; we recommend using the official SDK pinned to the quickstart sample. Tokenization differences are consistent across models but we'll provide sample scripts.
05:15 - Tom Rivera: Competitors — we currently evaluate OpenAI for hosted, and we've toyed with Anthropic for chat quality. Cohere for embeddings. How does Redwood differentiate for a startup like us?
05:28 - Maya Chen: Redwood focuses on production predictability: transparent latency/cost benchmarks, smart routing, and a unified experience between hosted and Dedicated/private options so you don't rewrite code when you scale. Also first-class observability for per-token cost and tracing.
05:42 - Priya Singh: Ok. On the billing side — how granular is usage reporting? We need per-route and per-team breakdowns.
05:49 - Arjun Patel: We expose token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and can integrate with your billing export or send daily usage reports.
06:00 - Sara Kim: Timeline — we want to run a one-week pilot starting the week of April 20th, results by the 27th, and then decide on Dedicated evaluation in early May. Is that feasible?
06:10 - Maya Chen: Yes, that's doable. We'll get the free credits and pilot keys to you within 2 business days after this call, pending legal/TOU acceptance.
06:18 - Tom Rivera: Any legal hurdles for the pilot? NDA?
06:20 - Maya Chen: For PLG self-serve pilot, standard terms apply. If you need an MSA or tighter terms, our legal team can fast-track a pilot MSA. For Private/Dedicated we'll go through enterprise contracting.
06:33 - Priya Singh: Great. Can you also include a sample prompt evaluation harness? We have a set of 400 prompts we want to run for quality checks.
06:39 - Arjun Patel: We'll share a benchmark harness; we can accept a CSV of prompts and expected responses and run automated quality diff and latency numbers.
06:49 - Sara Kim: Sounds good. Anything else?
06:52 - Maya Chen: I'll summarize the next steps.
06:55 - Maya Chen: Action items recap: Maya to send quickstart, credits and pricing; Arjun to share security pack + infra diagram and benchmark harness; Priya to send prompt set and traffic profile. We'll target pilot start week of April 20th.
07:12 - Tom Rivera: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
07:15 - Priya Singh: Thanks.
07:18 - Maya Chen: Thanks all, talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings, speaker overlaps around 02:30, some technical terms transcribed oddly ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Delighted" instead of Dedicated in one spot).

End of transcript.
